requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) is configured to route traffic between lan-a (node2, 10.50.1.0/24) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.2.0/24) using pure routing (no NAT), so packets traverse node1 with source addresses preserved.
requirements.summary: node1's eth1/eth2 were assigned static addresses on each LAN, ip_forward and per-interface forwarding were confirmed enabled, and a forward-filter firewall (default-drop, explicit accept for established/related plus lan-a<->lan-b/lan-b<->lan-a) was committed and saved. 'show nat source rules' explicitly reports no NAT configured. tcpdump captured on node3's LAN interface shows ICMP and TCP traffic arriving with source 10.50.1.11 (node2's real address), confirming no address translation occurred end-to-end, both before and after a full restart of node1.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port (not just a fixed allow-listed service), with both ICMP and arbitrary TCP ports functioning bidirectionally.
requirements.summary: ICMP connectivity between node2 (10.50.1.11) and node3 (10.50.2.12) succeeded immediately after static routes were added. An arbitrary TCP port (8765) initially failed due to host-level firewalld default zone blocking non-SSH ports on the LAN NIC (unrelated to node1's routing/firewall, which already permitted the traffic per the forward-filter hit counters). After trusting the LAN interface in firewalld on both nodes, arbitrary-port TCP succeeded in both directions (node2->node3:8765 and node3->node2:9999, both http_code=200), and a further arbitrary port (7777) was verified after node1's restart with tcpdump confirming successful three-way handshake and preserved source address.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 have durable/persistent routing to reach the opposite LAN via node1 (not merely transient manual configuration).
requirements.summary: Static addresses and routes on node2/node3 were configured via persistent NetworkManager connection profiles (autoconnect yes) rather than transient 'ip addr'/'ip route' commands, and node1's interface addressing and firewall rules were committed and saved to VyOS's persistent config. All configuration was independently verified to survive a full reboot of each of the three nodes with a changed boot_id and re-confirmed addresses, routes, firewall rules, and live cross-LAN ping.

overall_summary: node1 was configured as a stateful, non-NAT router between lan-a and lan-b, with tcpdump directly confirming original source addresses are preserved end-to-end for both ICMP and arbitrary TCP ports in both directions. Node2 and node3 reach each other on arbitrary ports after the executor also relaxed local firewalld zones (a necessary, evidence-justified but out-of-scope host change). All three nodes underwent a full sequential restart with matching pre/post boot_id changes (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots) and confirmed recovery of routing, firewall, and connectivity state, giving strong confidence in durability of the configuration.
limitations: The 'any port' requirement was only exercised with a small set of specific TCP ports (7777, 8765, 9999) plus ICMP, not an exhaustive port sweep; this is reasonable sampling but not literally 'any' port.

The task contract concerns only node1's routing behavior; the firewalld zone change on node2/node3 was necessary to observe the full outcome but falls outside strict scope of 'configure node1', slightly lowering hygiene confidence.

Restart evidence protocol is independent of the public task contract per instructions; it was fully and coherently captured for all three nodes and is used here only to raise confidence in durability, not as a scored task requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were mostly discovery, corrective, or evidence-bounded. A malformed firewall rule 5 (invalid 'state ... enable' syntax, cmd-bb38be2a3f594767) failed and was diagnosed via read-only find/cat commands, then cleanly deleted and recommitted with correct syntax (cmd-3cffa0ae594d45cf, cmd-3df37b217efb415c) — a legitimate self-correction. Early scratch addressing on node2/node3 (cmd-4fb2940749c8439c added an extraneous 10.50.2.11/24 address to node2's LAN NIC while probing which interface reached node1; it was promptly removed via cmd-403b21edf3224d27) and transient 'ip addr add' probes on node3 (cmd-a4dd71449a5643fa, cmd-16318bd5edbc498f) were superseded by the final persistent NetworkManager profiles, leaving no incorrect residue. Ad-hoc HTTP test servers on node2/node3 (ports 7777/8765/9999) were all explicitly killed after use (cmd-a9818543f8cb4342, cmd-054a4692c62a4088, embedded pkill in cmd-f42421c9617544d7), leaving only small /tmp log files (http.log, http2.log, tcpdump.log, reboot.log) as low-severity residue on node2/node3, visible in the after-executor snapshot. The executor also changed node2's and node3's firewalld zone for the LAN interface from 'public' to 'trusted' (cmd-aaffb09323e94770, cmd-b5612daaa6e843f9), which broadens the host-level firewall posture on that interface; this was a bounded, evidence-driven fix directly required to demonstrate the task's 'any port' requirement (the local host firewall, not node1, was blocking non-SSH traffic) and was retained deliberately, but it is host-level security relaxation beyond node1 configuration that was not explicitly requested and should be flagged.
